nodes.label: docs/canon/REVIEW_WORKLIST.md — one row per claim, ordered by enforcement power. REVIEW_REGISTER.md cuts the pile by file; this one cuts it by claim, the unit that actually costs something, because a claim is what an agent reads and then enforces. A file is neither true nor false; a claim is. The list appears in its own list as W-E58

The five tiers plus block decisions, ordered by how much work a wrong claim misdirects before anyone notices, not by how wrong it looks: Tier 1 CLAUDE.md, 50 rows, loads every session for every agent; Tier 2 the 25 live laptop memory files, 70 rows, same reach and less scrutiny; Tier 3 the 10 .claude/agents/*.md definitions, 50 rows, hard rules the instant an agent spawns and the worst grounded-to-invented ratio in the repo; Tier 4 v3/README.md, 28 rows, carrying a `## Decided` heading that makes every line under it a canon claim; Tier 5 everything else, 40 rows; Block B, 6 rows proposing block decisions for the 85 memory copies and 57 legacy worktree docs

The worklist's columns: id (stable, cite it in verdicts); surface (the file the claim is asserted in, file-level, with file:line where the line is load-bearing); claim (quoted verbatim as that surface states it, with ellipsis marking removed connective text only, never a qualifier); kind (intent — a claim about what the user wanted — or state — a claim about what exists, what a number is, what the code does — the distinction deciding what can settle it); check (something runnable: a CQ corpus search, a git command, or a code path with line numbers, never "see the audit"); audit prior (CANON_AUDIT.md's verdict where one exists, marked as one agent's opinion carrying no weight); status (every row starts `unreviewed`, only the user changes it)

The CQ corpus search, defined once per session in bash or PowerShell: it reads docs/canon/raw/user_turns_all.jsonl, regex-matches each turn's text case-insensitively, and prints the corpus line number, the timestamp and the turn text, then a `-> N hit(s)` total. The line number is what a verdict cites. `rg` is not on the bash PATH on this machine, so checks must not assume it. Zero hits is a real result and must be reported as such — it is not proof the user never said it

Two things that will bite whoever works the list. The corpus blackouts: the corpus is 920 turns 2026-05-14 → 2026-08-05 and the rows were written against the 803 extant on 08-03; nothing survives before 05-14 and 05-16 → 05-26 and 05-29 → 06-26 hold zero turns, so a claim whose only support sits there returns zero hits by construction and is cannot-determine, never unsupported — two quotes CANON_AUDIT.md cites with 06-25 dates return zero hits for exactly this reason. And the four data files are off limits, with rows whose natural check would open one marked [user-gated]: propose the check, do not run it

Tier 1 covers CLAUDE.md in 50 claims across six groups: 1a the banner and repo-layout claims, 1b session entry point and trust ordering, 1c the graphify rules, 1d hard rules, 1e the agent roster section, 1f the artefact-arm section. 20 of the 50 carry an audit prior and 30 are new to the list — CLAUDE.md was rewritten on 2026-08-03 after the audit read it, and the rewrite added a whole epistemics layer that nothing has checked

Tier 2 covers the 25 live laptop memory files in 70 claims, grouped as 2a MEMORY.md (the index — the part actually skimmed), 2b the behavioural entries (feedback_*), 2c the design and vocabulary entries, 2d the environment entries, 2e the results entries where the numbers live

Tier 3 covers the 10 agent definitions in 50 claims, grouped as 3a present in all ten definitions, 3b the terminology rule (six definitions), 3c the metric-validity table declared binding (five definitions), 3d pre-registered bars and closed findings, 3e design claims propagated into enforced rules, 3f method and behaviour rules

Tier 5 covers everything inert until someone opens it, in 40 claims: 5a v3/artefact/DESIGN.md + MODEL_CONTRACTS.md (15), 5b desktop-memory claims (12 rows covering 30 audit claims), 5c the state docs (8), 5d the docs/canon/ documents themselves (5)
